 home.insertBefore(card,home.querySelector('.how')||home.firstElementChild);
 card.querySelectorAll('[data-v22-start]').forEach(b=>b.onclick=()=>v22Begin(b.dataset.v22Start,$('v22SubjectPick').value));
 v22UpdateButtons();
}

');let button=alt.querySelector('#guideDeep');if(button)button.textContent='Open the full '+V21_NARRATIVES[v21TrailSubject].label+' course →';}

importNotebook=async function(file){if(!file)return;let memory=null;try{const value=JSON.parse(await file.text());if(value.remember&&typeof value.remember==='object'&&!Array.isArray(value.remember))memory=value.remember}catch{};

  const m=key.match(/^(spanish|chess|piano|life|medicine|business|books):(\d+)$/);
  if(!m||Number(m[2])>=v21Items(m[1]).length||!obj||!Number.isFinite(Number(obj.due)))continue;
  restored[key]={gap:Math.max(1,Math.min(60,Number(obj.gap)||1)),due:Number(obj.due),seen:Math.max(1,Number(obj.seen)||1),last:Number(obj.last)||Date.now(),level:['again','almost','clear'].includes(obj.level)?obj.level:'almost'};count++;
 }

 }
};

They need to examine the most forcing replies.","rule":"For each candidate move, ask: what is my opponent’s strongest check, capture or threat? Strong moves survive adversarial replies, not merely the variations you hope the opponent chooses.","evidence":"Write two short variations from an actual game, then compare with the full chess studio’s analysis.","misconception":"Do not assume your opponent will cooperate with a plan.","next_step":"Next: turn tactical habits into positional planning.","fen":"r3k2r/ppp2ppp/2n1bn2/3qp3/3PP3/2N2N2/PPP2PPP/R1BQ1RK1 w kq - 0 9","move":"e4d5"},{"stage":5,"title":"Make a plan you can explain","goal":"Balance threats, activity and king safety","hook":"The leap from beginner to intermediate play is choosing moves for reasons, not because they look familiar.","rule":"Evaluate king safety, material, piece activity, pawn structure and immediate threats. Make a plan that responds to the biggest imbalance; review it after every opponent move.","example":"If your opponent has an isolated pawn, you may blockade it, trade active pieces, then attack the weakness in the endgame.","question":"What should you do when the opponent makes a surprising move?","choices":["Continue your original plan without looking","Recheck threats and reassess the position","Always trade queens","Move the same piece twice"],"answer":1,"hint":"A plan is conditional on what the board actually says now.","steps":["Identify the opponent’s new threat, if any.","Re-evaluate tactics and positional changes.","Update your plan using the new evidence."],"reason":"Chess strategy is dynamic. A good plan is a hypothesis about a position and must adapt when the opponent changes its assumptions.","evidence":"Annotate a real game: for each move, state what you expected and which reply changed your judgment.","misconception":"A plan is not a memorized sequence of moves irrespective of replies.","next_step":"Next: return to the full Chess course for openings, deeper endgames and serious calculation.","fen":"r1bq1rk1/ppp2ppp/2n1pn2/3p4/3P4/2PBPN2/PP3PPP/RNBQ1RK1 w - - 2 8","move":"b1d2"}],"calculus":[{"stage":1,"title":"What does a slope tell you?","goal":"Describe change without calculus jargon","hook":"Imagine a bike moving 30 meters over 10 seconds. You already understand the idea behind a derivative.","rule":"Average rate of change = change in output ÷ change in input. Distance over time gives average speed; a line’s slope tells you how quickly y changes with x.","example":"30 meters in 10 seconds = 3 meters per second.","question":"A cyclist travels 48 meters in 12 seconds. What is average speed?","choices":["2 m/s","4 m/s","12 m/s","576 m/s"],"answer":1,"hint":"Divide the total change in distance by the total time.","steps":["Write rate = distance ÷ time.","Substitute 48 ÷ 12.","The result is 4 meters per second."],"reason":"A rate is a ratio of changes. Its units come from dividing the output unit by the input unit: meters/seconds.","evidence":"Measure two points on a distance-time graph; the slope of the line joining them gives average speed.","misconception":"Distance ÷ time is not the same as instantaneous speed if velocity changes.","next_step":"Next: find the speed at one exact moment.","visual":"slope"},{"stage":1,"title":"Instantaneous change","goal":"See what a derivative is doing","hook":"A car’s dashboard shows speed now, not its speed averaged over the whole journey.","rule":"To estimate the rate at one instant, measure change over shorter and shorter intervals near that instant. The derivative is the limit of these slopes when the limit exists.","example":"If position is s(t)=t², average speed from t=2 to 2+h is ((2+h)²−4)/h = 4+h. As h approaches 0, speed approaches 4.","question":"For s(t)=t², what is the instantaneous speed at t=3?","choices":["3","6","9","12"],"answer":1,"hint":"The derivative of t² is 2t; evaluate it at t=3.","steps":["Take a nearby average slope: ((3+h)²−9)/h.","Expand: (9+6h+h²−9)/h = 6+h.","As h→0, that approaches 6."],"reason":"The limit removes the dependence on interval width. You are not dividing by zero; you examine nonzero h values arbitrarily close to zero.","evidence":"Compute nearby slopes at h=1, 0.1, 0.01 and watch them converge to 6.","misconception":"A derivative need not exist at a corner or jump.","next_step":"Next: connect this intuition to a general rule.","visual":"slope"},{"stage":2,"title":"The power rule","goal":"Differentiate x³ without memorizing magic","hook":"Patterns that arise from the limit definition make a powerful shortcut.","rule":"For integer n≥1, d(xⁿ)/dx = n xⁿ⁻¹. Constants differentiate to zero; constants multiplying a function stay in front.","example":"d(3x² + 5x)/dx = 6x + 5.","question":"What is d(x³)/dx?","choices":["x²","3x²","3x³","x⁴"],"answer":1,"hint":"Bring the exponent down, then subtract one from it.","steps":["The power is 3.","Multiply the coefficient 1 by 3.","Lower the power to 2: 3x²."],"reason":"Expanding (x+h)ⁿ and taking the limit shows that the first-order term is n xⁿ⁻¹; higher powers of h vanish as h→0.","evidence":"Derive d(x²)/dx using (x+h)²−x² over h to see the underlying pattern.","misconception":"The power rule is not applied directly to products of unrelated functions; use the product rule there.","next_step":"Next: find where a curve is rising or falling.","visual":"slope"},{"stage":2,"title":"Read a derivative graphically","goal":"Find increasing and decreasing regions","hook":"Sometimes you do not need a calculator; a derivative tells you the direction a function is moving.","rule":"If f′(x)>0, the function increases locally. If f′(x)<0, it decreases. At f′(x)=0 the graph may have a peak, valley, or a flat inflection.","example":"For f(x)=x², f′(x)=2x. To the left of zero the slope is negative; to the right it is positive.","question":"For f(x)=x², what is true at x=−2?","choices":["The slope is positive","The slope is zero","The slope is negative","The function is undefined"],"answer":2,"hint":"Evaluate 2x at a negative x.","steps":["Differentiate x² to get 2x.","Substitute x=−2, giving −4.","A negative slope means the graph is decreasing there."],"reason":"The tangent slope captures local direction. A negative derivative is not a negative function value: f(−2)=4 while f′(−2)=−4.","evidence":"Slide the point along the parabola and compare the direction of its tangent line.","misconception":"Zero derivative does not always mean maximum or minimum; x³ is flat at zero but keeps increasing.","next_step":"Next: optimize something real.","visual":"slope"},{"stage":3,"title":"Find a maximum","goal":"Use derivatives to make a practical decision","hook":"You have 20 meters of fencing for a rectangular garden. Which shape encloses the most area?","rule":"If sides are x and 10−x, area A=x(10−x)=10x−x². Differentiate: A′=10−2x. Set A′=0 and check endpoints or concavity.","example":"The maximum occurs at x=5, making a 5×5 square with area 25 m².","question":"Which side lengths maximize area with perimeter 20 m?","choices":["2 m and 8 m","4 m and 6 m","5 m and 5 m","1 m and 9 m"],"answer":2,"hint":"Use the derivative of the area expression, not just intuition about rectangles.","steps":["Perimeter 2x+2y=20, so y=10−x.","Area A=10x−x². Set derivative 10−2x=0.","x=5, y=5; compare the endpoints to confirm the maximum."],"reason":"At an interior optimum of a smooth function, the slope often becomes zero. Testing curvature and boundaries distinguishes a maximum from a minimum.","evidence":"Try several candidate rectangles and compute their areas; derivative calculus confirms the pattern.","misconception":"Not every critical point is a global maximum.","next_step":"Next: understand how two functions combine.","visual":"slope"},{"stage":3,"title":"The chain rule","goal":"Differentiate a function inside a function","hook":"You already know how to differentiate x². What if the input is 3x+1 rather than just x?","rule":"The chain rule says: differentiate the outside, keep the inside, then multiply by the derivative of the inside.","example":"For y=(3x+1)², y′=2(3x+1)·3 = 6(3x+1).","question":"What is d[(2x+1)³]/dx?","choices":["3(2x+1)²","6(2x+1)²","(2x+1)²","6(2x+1)³"],"answer":1,"hint":"The outside cube gives 3 times the square; the inside 2x+1 contributes an extra 2.","steps":["Outside derivative: 3(2x+1)².","Differentiate the inside: d(2x+1)/dx = 2.","Multiply: 6(2x+1)²."],"reason":"For tiny changes, the outside change per inside-unit is multiplied by the inside change per x-unit: rates multiply.","evidence":"Try expanding (2x+1)³ and differentiating term by term; you get the same result.","misconception":"Forgetting the inner derivative is the standard trap.","next_step":"Next: learn the other half of calculus.","visual":"slope"},{"stage":3,"title":"Area as accumulation","goal":"Understand an integral without mystery","hook":"Imagine water flowing into a tub. The amount added depends on the flow rate and how long it runs.","rule":"A definite integral adds up small contributions: rate × tiny interval. Graphically, it gives signed area under a rate-versus-time curve.","example":"A constant flow of 3 liters/minute for 4 minutes adds 12 liters: ∫₀⁴ 3 dt = 12.","question":"A tap supplies 5 liters/minute for 6 minutes. How much water is added?","choices":["5 liters","11 liters","30 liters","60 liters"],"answer":2,"hint":"Area of a rectangle under a constant-rate graph = height × width.","steps":["Rate is 5 L/min.","Duration is 6 min.","Multiply to get 30 liters; the minutes cancel."],"reason":"An integral is a limit of sums. Cut the interval into many narrow strips, add strip areas, then make them arbitrarily narrow.","evidence":"Draw a horizontal rate line and count the rectangular area underneath; the same idea works for curved graphs using thinner slices.","misconception":"For negative rates, a definite integral can represent net change rather than total positive activity.","next_step":"Next: connect accumulation and derivatives.","visual":"area"},{"stage":4,"title":"The fundamental theorem","goal":"See why derivatives and integrals fit together","hook":"Differentiation tells you the rate of change. Integration reconstructs accumulated change.","rule":"The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus links them: if F′=f, then ∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx = F(b)−F(a), under the usual continuity assumptions.","example":"For f(x)=2x, choose F(x)=x². Then ∫₀³2x dx=3²−0²=9.","question":"What is ∫₀² 2x dx?","choices":["2","4","6","8"],"answer":1,"hint":"An antiderivative of 2x is x². Evaluate at the endpoints.","steps":["Integrate 2x to x².","Evaluate upper endpoint: 2²=4.","Subtract lower endpoint: 0²=0. Total 4."],"reason":"The theorem explains why accumulation of instantaneous rates reconstructs change. It is not two unrelated sets of tricks.","evidence":"Approximate the area under y=2x with narrow rectangles, then compare with the exact triangular area ½×2×4=4.","misconception":"Remember to subtract lower endpoint; an indefinite integral also needs an arbitrary constant.","next_step":"Next: understand approximation and modeling.","visual":"area"},{"stage":4,"title":"When an exact formula is impossible","goal":"Approximate an integral","hook":"Real data often arrives as measurements, not a neat equation. Calculus still works.","rule":"Numerical integration approximates area by rectangles or trapezoids. Accuracy generally improves as intervals shrink for sufficiently regular functions.","example":"If speeds at t=0,1,2 are 0,2,4 m/s, trapezoids over each one-second interval estimate 1+3=4 meters.","question":"Using trapezoids, what is the estimated area under a straight line from (0,0) to (2,4)?","choices":["2","4","6","8"],"answer":1,"hint":"This is a triangle. The trapezoidal rule is exact for a straight line.","steps":["Average endpoint heights: (0+4)/2=2.","Multiply by width 2.","Area = 4."],"reason":"Trapezoids replace a curve with straight segments. Error depends on curvature and step width; real measurements also carry uncertainty.","evidence":"Compare rectangles and trapezoids on a hand-drawn graph to see why different approximations differ.","misconception":"Using rectangles is an approximation, not an algebra error. The size and placement of the strips affect the result.","next_step":"Next: take derivatives with multiple variables.","visual":"area"},{"stage":5,"title":"Two variables, two kinds of slope","goal":"Understand partial derivatives","hook":"Temperature changes as you walk east or north. Which direction are you measuring?","rule":"A partial derivative measures change in one input while holding others fixed. For f(x,y)=x²+3y, ∂f/∂x=2x and ∂f/∂y=3.","example":"At x=2, a small step in x changes f at a rate near 4 units per x-unit; in y, the rate is 3.","question":"For f(x,y)=x²+3y, what is ∂f/∂y?","choices":["x²","2x","3","3y"],"answer":2,"hint":"Treat x as fixed when taking the derivative with respect to y.","steps":["Hold x constant, so x² acts like a constant.","Differentiate 3y with respect to y.","The result is 3."],"reason":"The gradient collects partial derivatives and points in the direction of fastest local increase for ordinary Euclidean coordinates.","evidence":"Check a tiny y-change: f(x,y+0.01)−f(x,y)=0.03, then divide by 0.01 to obtain 3.","misconception":"The partial derivative with respect to x is not the same as the one with respect to y.","next_step":"Next: explore the full Calculus Arcade for multivariable and applied calculus.","visual":"slope"}],"physics":[{"stage":1,"title":"Why do objects fall?","goal":"Predict falling motion","hook":"Drop a heavy ball and a light ball in a vacuum from the same height. It is tempting to expect the heavier one to win.","rule":"Near Earth’s surface, neglecting air resistance, both accelerate downward at approximately 9.8 m/s². Gravity pulls harder on greater mass, but greater mass also means more inertia.","example":"On the Moon, Apollo 15 astronaut David Scott dropped a hammer and a feather together; with almost no air, they landed together.","question":"In a vacuum, which falls faster from the same height?","choices":["The heavier ball","The lighter ball","They accelerate equally","Whichever has more surface area"],"answer":2,"hint":"Separate gravity from air resistance. Ask what happens if there is no drag.","steps":["Gravitational force near Earth: F≈mg.","Newton’s second law: acceleration a=F/m.","The mass cancels: a≈g, independent of the object’s mass."],"reason":"This equal-acceleration principle is experimentally supported to high precision and was central to later thinking about equivalence in gravity.","evidence":"Repeat the thought experiment with no air and compare to a feather falling in air. The difference is drag, not gravitational acceleration.","misconception":"In air, two objects with different shapes can fall very differently.","next_step":"Next: relate speed and acceleration.","visual":"fall"},{"stage":1,"title":"Speed is not acceleration","goal":"Understand changes in motion","hook":"A car moving at 60 mph at a constant rate can have zero acceleration. A slow car speeding up can have a large acceleration.","rule":"Velocity measures motion per unit time; acceleration measures change in velocity per unit time. You can accelerate by changing speed or direction.","example":"A car goes from 0 to 20 m/s in 5 seconds: average acceleration = (20−0)/5 = 4 m/s².","question":"A car changes speed from 4 m/s to 16 m/s in 3 seconds. What is average acceleration?","choices":["3 m/s²","4 m/s²","12 m/s²","48 m/s²"],"answer":1,"hint":"Find the change in velocity, then divide by elapsed time.","steps":["Velocity change = 16−4=12 m/s.","Time = 3 seconds.","Acceleration = 12/3 = 4 m/s²."],"reason":"The units are m/s per s, or m/s². A curved path can have acceleration even at constant speed because direction changes.","evidence":"Watch a vehicle turn steadily; the speedometer may stay fixed while its velocity vector turns.","misconception":"Acceleration does not mean only “getting faster.”","next_step":"Next: understand what forces do.","visual":"motion"},{"stage":1,"title":"Newton’s second law","goal":"Predict what a force changes","hook":"Push an empty shopping cart and a heavily loaded one with the same force. One speeds up more.","rule":"For constant mass, net force F=ma. Acceleration grows with net force and shrinks with mass. The word net matters: opposite forces can cancel.","example":"With 10 newtons net force on a 2 kg cart: a=10/2=5 m/s².","question":"What acceleration does a 12 N net force produce on a 3 kg object?","choices":["3 m/s²","4 m/s²","9 m/s²","36 m/s²"],"answer":1,"hint":"Rearrange F=ma into a=F/m.","steps":["Write acceleration = net force / mass.","Substitute 12 N / 3 kg.","Result 4 m/s²."],"reason":"Newton’s laws provide a model for relating measurable forces and motion over ordinary speeds and scales. They were supported by astronomical and terrestrial observations.","evidence":"Change the cart’s mass and predict acceleration with the same push; controlled experiments test the inverse relationship.","misconception":"A body can move with zero net force; it just will not accelerate.","next_step":"Next: energy explains motion another way.","visual":"motion"},{"stage":2,"title":"Energy can change form","goal":"Track potential and kinetic energy","hook":"A roller coaster climbs, slows, and then speeds up as it descends.","rule":"Gravitational potential energy near Earth is mgh. Kinetic energy is ½mv². Ignoring losses, the sum stays constant: falling converts potential into kinetic energy.","example":"A 2 kg object raised 5 m gains about 2×9.8×5≈98 joules of gravitational potential energy.","question":"Ignoring air resistance, when a roller coaster descends, what usually increases?","choices":["Its gravitational potential energy","Its kinetic energy","Its mass","Its total mechanical energy"],"answer":1,"hint":"Height falls, speed rises; which stored form becomes motion?","steps":["Descending reduces height and gravitational potential energy.","The energy goes into motion when losses are neglected.","Kinetic energy therefore increases."],"reason":"Conservation principles make predictions without resolving every instant of force; energy accounting is a different powerful lens on motion.","evidence":"Track speed and height along a track and compare ½mv²+mgh at different points.","misconception":"Friction does not destroy energy; it converts mechanical energy into heat and other forms.","next_step":"Next: learn momentum and collisions.","visual":"energy"},{"stage":2,"title":"Momentum survives a collision","goal":"Explain recoil and collisions","hook":"Why does a skateboard roll backward if you throw a heavy ball forward while standing on it?","rule":"Momentum p=mv is conserved in an isolated system: total momentum before equals total afterward. Forces internal to the system come in equal and opposite pairs.","example":"If a 2 kg object moves at 3 m/s, its momentum is 6 kg·m/s.","question":"What is the momentum of a 4 kg cart moving at 2 m/s?","choices":["2 kg·m/s","6 kg·m/s","8 kg·m/s","16 kg·m/s"],"answer":2,"hint":"Multiply mass by velocity.","steps":["Write p=mv.","Multiply 4 kg × 2 m/s.","Result 8 kg·m/s in the direction of motion."],"reason":"Momentum conservation follows from Newton’s laws for isolated systems and remains foundational in modern physics with appropriate relativistic generalization.","evidence":"In low-friction cart experiments, add momenta before and after a collision and compare.","misconception":"Momentum has direction; opposite velocities can cancel in the system total.","next_step":"Next: see how a simple electric circuit works.","visual":"motion"},{"stage":2,"title":"Build a circuit in your head","goal":"Understand voltage, current and resistance","hook":"A battery and a bulb are useless if the circuit is open. Electricity needs a complete conducting path.","rule":"Voltage is energy transferred per unit charge, current is charge flow per second, and resistance opposes current. For ohmic components, V=IR.","example":"A 6 V battery across a 3 Ω resistor yields I=6/3=2 A, if the resistor obeys Ohm’s law.","question":"Across a 4 Ω resistor, what current flows when voltage is 12 V?","choices":["3 A","4 A","8 A","48 A"],"answer":0,"hint":"Use I=V/R.","steps":["Write Ohm’s law: V=IR.","Solve I=V/R.","Calculate 12/4 = 3 amperes."],"reason":"Ohm’s law is an empirical relation for suitable components under roughly fixed physical conditions; not every device behaves as a simple resistor.","evidence":"Compare several resistors in a basic circuit simulator and see how current changes when voltage is held fixed.","misconception":"Current does not get “used up” in a simple series circuit; energy is transferred in components.","next_step":"Next: follow a wave.","visual":"circuit"},{"stage":3,"title":"How waves carry information","goal":"Tell frequency from amplitude","hook":"You hear two notes: one is louder and one is higher in pitch. Those are not the same property.","rule":"Frequency counts cycles per second and is measured in hertz. Amplitude measures size of oscillation. For sound, frequency relates to pitch; amplitude relates to loudness (along with perception).","example":"A tuning fork vibrating 440 times per second produces a 440 Hz tone.","question":"Which change generally makes a musical note higher in pitch?","choices":["Increasing amplitude only","Increasing frequency","Decreasing temperature only","Increasing the instrument’s mass"],"answer":1,"hint":"Pitch follows the number of vibration cycles per second.","steps":["Count how many complete cycles happen each second.","More cycles each second means higher frequency.","Higher frequency generally means higher perceived pitch."],"reason":"Wave behavior is confirmed by microphones, oscilloscopes and frequency analysis. Human pitch perception is related to frequency but more complex for rich sounds.","evidence":"Sing a high note quietly and a low note loudly: amplitude and frequency can vary independently.","misconception":"Louder does not mean higher in pitch.","next_step":"Next: understand pressure and heat.","visual":"wave"},{"stage":3,"title":"Heat flows, temperature measures","goal":"Avoid the everyday-language trap","hook":"A hot cup of coffee cools because energy moves to cooler surroundings.","rule":"Temperature relates to thermal state; heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference. Objects do not “contain heat” as a thermodynamic state variable.","example":"A metal spoon feels cold partly because it conducts thermal energy from your hand faster than wood at the same temperature.","question":"What is heat in thermodynamics?","choices":["A substance trapped in warm things","Energy transferred due to a temperature difference","The number of atoms in an object","Exactly the same thing as temperature"],"answer":1,"hint":"Heat describes energy moving between systems, not a temperature reading.","steps":["Identify two systems at different temperatures.","Energy transfer driven by that difference is heat.","The process tends toward thermal equilibrium in an isolated combined system."],"reason":"Thermodynamics grew from experiments on engines, calorimetry and energy conservation; heat was established as energy transfer rather than a caloric fluid.","evidence":"Touch metal and wood at the same room temperature and notice different heat-transfer rates.","misconception":"High temperature and high total internal energy are not synonymous.","next_step":"Next: see why engines have limits.","visual":"heat"},{"stage":3,"title":"Why no engine is perfectly efficient","goal":"Understand entropy intuitively","hook":"A car engine cannot turn every joule of fuel energy into useful motion.","rule":"The second law of thermodynamics constrains which energy transfers are possible. For a heat engine, some energy must generally be rejected to a colder reservoir.","example":"A perfect engine converting all absorbed heat into work while exchanging heat with only one reservoir is impossible for a cyclic heat engine.","question":"Why must a heat engine generally reject some energy as waste heat?","choices":["The second law limits conversion of heat into work","Gravity destroys part of the fuel","Energy conservation is false","The engine creates mass from nothing"],"answer":0,"hint":"Think about the second law, not a failure of energy conservation.","steps":["A heat engine takes energy from a hot source.","To operate cyclically, it must reject some energy to a cooler sink.","The second law forbids 100% conversion of the absorbed heat into work in this setup."],"reason":"Carnot’s analysis of ideal engines showed that efficiency depends on hot and cold reservoir temperatures; experiments confirmed these limits.","evidence":"Compute an ideal Carnot upper bound η=1−Tc/Th in kelvin for sample temperatures.","misconception":"Not every device called an “engine” is a heat engine; electric motors have different efficiency constraints.","next_step":"Next: see what changes at high speed.","visual":"heat"},{"stage":4,"title":"What relativity actually changes","goal":"Explain time dilation without science fiction","hook":"Two observers moving relative to each other do not always agree about elapsed times between separated events.","rule":"Special relativity keeps the speed of light in vacuum constant for inertial observers. Moving clocks are observed to run slower by factor γ=1/√(1−v²/c²) when compared in the appropriate frame.","example":"At 0.6c, γ=1.25. A journey lasting 4 years on the traveling clock corresponds to 5 years in the Earth frame for a simple constant-speed segment.","question":"At 0.6 times light speed, what is γ approximately?","choices":["1.0","1.25","1.6","2.0"],"answer":1,"hint":"Compute 1/sqrt(1−0.6²)=1/sqrt(0.64).","steps":["Square 0.6: 0.36.","1−0.36=0.64, whose square root is 0.8.","1/0.8=1.25."],"reason":"Muon lifetimes, particle accelerators and precision clock experiments confirm relativistic time effects. This is experimentally measured, not merely hypothetical.","evidence":"Compare proper time along two different spacetime paths rather than asking whose clock is “really” slow without specifying observations.","misconception":"Time dilation does not mean all observers universally agree that one particular clock is slow.","next_step":"Next: learn why quantum physics is probabilistic.","visual":"light"},{"stage":4,"title":"A photon is not a tiny marble","goal":"Understand quantized light","hook":"Very dim light still arrives in discrete detector clicks.","rule":"Photon energy is E=hf, where h is Planck’s constant and f is light frequency. Light exhibits interference and diffraction, and individual detections are discrete.","example":"Blue light has a higher frequency than red light and therefore each blue photon carries more energy.","question":"Which light has more energy per photon: blue or red?","choices":["Red, because its wavelength is longer","Blue, because its frequency is higher","They are always identical","Whichever beam is brighter"],"answer":1,"hint":"Photon energy depends on frequency, not how many photons are in the beam.","steps":["Use E=hf.","Compare frequencies: blue exceeds red in visible light.","Each blue photon therefore carries greater energy."],"reason":"The photoelectric effect provided evidence that electron emission depends on frequency in a way classical wave intensity alone could not explain.","evidence":"Change light intensity at fixed low frequency in a photoelectric demonstration and compare it with changing frequency above threshold.","misconception":"Brighter light means more photon energy per photon only if frequency also changes—which brightness alone does not imply.","next_step":"Next: explore the full Physics foundations and medical physics lab.","visual":"light"}]};

function v23First(s){let rec=safeStore.get('v23:last',null);if(rec&&rec.subject===s&&Number.isInteger(rec.index))return rec.index;let due=V23_TRACKS[s].findIndex((_,i)=>v23IsDue(s,i));if(due>=0)return due;let fresh=V23_TRACKS[s].findIndex((_,i)=>!v23Storage()[s+':'+i]);return fresh>=0?fresh:Math.max(0,V23_TRACKS[s].length-1)}
function v23Name(s){return V23_NAMES[s]||s}
function v23Open(s,i=null){if(!READY||!V23_TRACKS[s])return;
 v22Session=null;v21TrailActive=false;v21HelpContext=null;v23PianoProgress=0;subject=s;v23Active={subject:s,index:Math.max(0,Math.min(V23_TRACKS[s].length-1,i==null?v23First(s):Number(i)||0))};
 safeStore.set('v23:last',v23Active);safeStore.set('v21:lastMode','v23');document.body.classList.remove('v21-guided');activePath='';drawMenu();updateTrail();v23Render();}
function v23Next(i){if(!v23Active)return;v23Open(v23Active.subject,i)}
function v23Renderable(t){return h(t||'').replace(/\n/g,'<br>')}
function v23HomeCards(){return Object.keys(V23_TRACKS).map(s=>{let n=v23Counts(s);return `<section class="v23-subject-card"><span class="v23-card-level">${n.done}/${V23_TRACKS[s].length} lessons visited</span><h3>${v23Name(s)}</h3><p>${h(V23_SKILLS[s])}</p><button type="button" class="v23-main" data-v23-start="${s}">${n.done?'Keep going':'Start with a quick win'} →</button><button type="button" class="v23-secondary" data-v23-full="${s}">Full course</button></section>`}).join('')}
const __v23OriginalGo=go;
go=function(path,opts={}){v23Active=null;return __v23OriginalGo(path,opts)};
const __v23OldBegin=v22Begin;
v22Begin=function(mode='easy',sub='all'){v23Active=null;return __v23OldBegin(mode,sub)};
const __v23OldHome=showHome;
showHome=function(){v23Active=null;__v23OldHome();if(!READY)return;
 const home=$('screen').querySelector('.v21-home');if(!home)return;
 const area=document.createElement('section');area.className='v23-entrance';area.innerHTML=`<div class="v23-entrance-top"><div><span class="eyebrow">A GOOD PLACE TO BEGIN</span><h2>Get the hang of it. The science and math courses have their own places in the subject menu now.</p>`;
 home.insertBefore(area,home.querySelector('.v22-feature')||home.firstElementChild);
 v23Wire(area);
 const foot=home.querySelector('.footnote');if(foot)foot.textContent='The original 216 files are preserved inside this HTML, including both PDFs. These new lessons add to the collection without replacing any course.';
 $('pageTitle').textContent='Your complete learning library';
};

function v23Render(){const {subject:s,index:i}=v23Active;const arr=V23_TRACKS[s],x=arr[i],p=v23Counts(s),done=v23Storage()[s+':'+i];
 $('pageTitle').textContent=v23Name(s)+' · '+x.title;$('status').textContent='Lesson '+(i+1)+' of '+arr.length+' · Everything in the original course is still available';

actual measurements have uncertainty.</p>':''}</main><aside class="v23-index"><div class="v23-index-intro"><strong>Your ${h(v23Name(s))} path</strong><span>${p.done} visited · ${p.due} worth revisiting</span></div><div class="v23-index-lessons">${lessons}</div>${p.due?'<button type="button" class="v23-review-button" id="v23ReviewDue">Revisit ' + p.due + ' idea' + (p.due===1?'':'s') + '</button>':''}<div class="v23-index-guide"><p><strong>Not sure where to start?</strong> Begin with lesson 1. You can always skip ahead or open the full studio.</p><button id="v23StartOver" type="button">Start at the beginning</button></div></aside></div></div>`;
 if($('v23ReviewDue'))$('v23ReviewDue').onclick=()=>v23Next(V23_TRACKS[s].findIndex((_,k)=>v23IsDue(s,k)));
 $('v23Home').onclick=showHome;$('v23Prev').onclick=()=>v23Next(i-1);$('v23Next').onclick=()=>v23Next(i+1);$('v23StartOver').onclick=()=>v23Next(0);
 $('v23Full').onclick=()=>go(V23_LINKS[s]);$('v23Complete').onclick=()=>{v23Save(s,i,'almost');$('v23Complete').textContent='✓ Explored';$('v23Rated').textContent='Saved. We can revisit this later.'};
 $('screen').querySelectorAll('[data-v23-index]').forEach(b=>b.onclick=()=>v23Next(+b.dataset.v23Index));$('screen').querySelectorAll('[data-v23-subject]').forEach(b=>b.onclick=()=>v23Open(b.dataset.v23Subject));
 $('v23Hint').onclick=()=>v23Feedback(x.hint);
 $('screen').querySelectorAll('[data-v23-option]').forEach(b=>b.onclick=()=>{let j=+b.dataset.v23Option,ok=j===x.answer;let all=$('v23Answers').querySelectorAll('button');all.forEach(q=>{q.classList.remove('v23-selected');q.setAttribute('aria-pressed','false')});b.classList.add('v23-selected');b.setAttribute('aria-pressed','true');v23Feedback(ok?'Yes. '+x.reason:'Not quite. '+x.hint+' You can try again, or reveal the steps.');if(ok){$('v23Reveal').hidden=false;v23Save(s,i,'almost')}});
 $('v23Show').onclick=()=>{$('v23Reveal').hidden=false;v23Feedback('Here is the answer and the reasoning behind it.');};

 $('screen').querySelectorAll('[data-v23-rate]').forEach(b=>b.onclick=()=>{let val=b.dataset.v23Rate;v23Save(s,i,val);$('screen').querySelectorAll('[data-v23-rate]').forEach(q=>{q.classList.toggle('v23-rated',q===b);q.setAttribute('aria-pressed',q===b?'true':'false')});$('v23Rated').textContent=val==='again'?'This will come back tomorrow.':val==='almost'?'This will come back in three days.':'This will come back in a week.';$('v23Complete').textContent='✓ Explored';});
 $('v23Ask').onclick=()=>v23AnswerQuestion($('v23Question').value);$('v23Question').onkeydown=e=>{if(e.key==='Enter'){e.preventDefault();v23AnswerQuestion(e.target.value)}};

}
function v23Feedback(text){$('v23Feedback').hidden=false;$('v23Feedback').textContent=text}
function v23AnswerQuestion(value){let q=String(value||'').trim().slice(0,400);if(!q)return;const {subject:s,index:i}=v23Active,x=V23_TRACKS[s][i],normalized=q.toLowerCase();
 let answer='';if(/(discover|figured|know|evidence|prove|experiment|why.*true|source)/i.test(normalized))answer=x.evidence;
 else if(/(simpl|begin|basic|zero|confus|lost|don't get|dont get|foundation)/i.test(normalized))answer=x.hook+'\n\n'+x.rule;
 else if(/(why|reason|how.*work|explain)/i.test(normalized))answer=x.reason+'\n\nStart with: '+x.steps[0];
 else if(/(step|walk|calculate|solve|derive|show)/i.test(normalized))answer=x.steps.map((t,j)=>(j+1)+'. '+t).join('\n');
 else if(/(example|use|real life)/i.test(normalized))answer=x.example+'\n\n'+x.evidence;
 else if(/(wrong|mistake|trap|instead)/i.test(normalized))answer=x.misconception+'\n\n'+x.rule;
 else if(/(answer|correct)/i.test(normalized))answer=x.choices[x.answer]+'\n\n'+x.reason;
 else answer='For this lesson, I can explain the underlying idea, walk through the calculation, show an example, or explain the evidence. Try “Why?” or “Show the steps.” For a question beyond this lesson, open the complete '+v23Name(s)+' course.';
 const box=$('v23CoachAnswer');box.hidden=false;box.innerHTML='<p class="v23-coach-prompt"><strong>You asked:</strong> '+h(q)+'</p><p>'+v23Renderable(answer)+'</p>';
}
function v23Interactive(s,x){if(s==='piano')return `<section class="v23-playground"><div class="v23-minihead"><span class="eyebrow">TRY IT ON THE KEYS</span><span>Tap the next highlighted note</span></div><div class="v23-note-seq">${(x.notes||[]).map((n,j)=>`<span data-v23-noteindex="${j}">${h(n.replace(/\d/,''))}</span>`).join('')}</div><div id="v23Keyboard" class="v23-keys" role="group" aria-label="Piano keys, C through next C"></div><p class="v23-mini-status" id="v23PianoStatus" role="status">Press the highlighted key to start. You can also follow along on a real keyboard.</p><button class="v23-mini-btn" id="v23Demo" type="button">Hear the notes</button><button class="v23-mini-btn" id="v23Replay" type="button">Try the notes again</button></section>`;
 if(s==='chess'&&x.fen)return `<section class="v23-playground"><div class="v23-minihead"><span class="eyebrow">SEE THE POSITION</span><span>White is at the bottom</span></div><div class="v23-board-wrap"><div class="v23-board" id="v23ChessBoard" role="group" aria-label="Chess position"></div><div><p id="v23SquareDescription" class="v23-mini-status">Tap any square to inspect it. These are lesson illustrations; play the full chess game in the complete course.</p></div></div></section>`;
 if(s==='calculus')return `<section class="v23-playground"><div class="v23-minihead"><span class="eyebrow">MAKE IT MOVE</span><span>${x.visual==='area'?'Accumulated area':'Slope of a curve'}</span></div><div class="v23-figure" id="v23Graph"></div><label for="v23MathSlider">${x.visual==='area'?'Number of small rectangles':'Move along the curve'} <strong id="v23MathVal"></strong></label><input id="v23MathSlider" type="range" min="${x.visual==='area'?2:-3}" max="${x.visual==='area'?30:3}" step="${x.visual==='area'?1:.25}" value="${x.visual==='area'?6:1}" /></section>`;
 if(s==='physics')return `<section class="v23-playground"><div class="v23-minihead"><span class="eyebrow">TRY AN EXPERIMENT</span><span>Change one thing and notice what follows</span></div><div class="v23-figure" id="v23PhysicsFigure"></div><label for="v23PhysicsSlider" id="v23PhysicsLabel">Adjust the experiment</label><input id="v23PhysicsSlider" type="range" min="1" max="10" step="1" value="5"/><p class="v23-mini-status" id="v23PhysicsReadout" role="status"></p></section>`;
 if(s==='spanish')return `<section class="v23-playground v23-speech"><span class="eyebrow">SAY IT OUT LOUD</span><p>${h(x.audio||x.example)}</p><button class="v23-mini-btn" id="v23Speak" type="button">Hear it in Spanish</button><p class="v23-mini-status" id="v23SpeakStatus" role="status">Try saying the phrase before listening.</p>${v23VerbsHtml()}</section>`;
 return '';
}
const __v23RenderOld=v23Render;
v23Render=function(){__v23RenderOld();if(v23Active?.subject==='chess')v23BindChess(V23_TRACKS.chess[v23Active.index]);if(v23Active?.subject==='spanish')v23BindSpanish(V23_TRACKS.spanish[v23Active.index])};
function v23BindSpanish(x){v23BindVerbs();$('v23Speak').onclick=()=>{try{if(!window.speechSynthesis)throw Error('Speech unavailable');window.speechSynthesis.cancel();let utterance=new SpeechSynthesisUtterance(x.audio||x.example);utterance.lang='es-MX';utterance.rate=.84;window.speechSynthesis.speak(utterance);$('v23SpeakStatus').textContent='Listen once, then repeat without looking.'}catch{$('v23SpeakStatus').textContent='Speech is not supported in this browser. You can still practise reading aloud.'}}}
function v23BindChess(x){let root=$('v23ChessBoard');if(!root)return;let glyph={K:'♔',Q:'♕',R:'♖',B:'♗',N:'♘',P:'♙',k:'♚',q:'♛',r:'♜',b:'♝',n:'♞',p:'♟'};let grid=[];for(let part of x.fen.split(' ')[0].split('/')){let row=[];for(let ch of part){if(/[1-8]/.test(ch))row.push(...Array(Number(ch)).fill(''));else row.push(ch)}grid.push(...row)};if(grid.length!==64)return;root.innerHTML=grid.map((piece,i)=>{let square='abcdefgh'[i%8]+(8-Math.floor(i/8));return `<button type="button" class="v23-square ${(Math.floor(i/8)+i%8)%2?'dark':''}" aria-label="${square}: ${piece?(piece===piece.toUpperCase()?'White':'Black'):''} ${piece?({k:'king',q:'queen',r:'rook',b:'bishop',n:'knight',p:'pawn'}[piece.toLowerCase()]):'empty'}" data-v23-square="${square}">${glyph[piece]||''}${i%8===0?'<small>'+ (8-Math.floor(i/8))+'</small>':''}</button>`}).join('');root.querySelectorAll('button').forEach(b=>b.onclick=()=>{$('v23SquareDescription').textContent=b.getAttribute('aria-label')+'. Take a moment to see which other squares that piece could affect.'})}
function v23BindPiano(x){const white=['C4','D4','E4','F4','G4','A4','B4','C5'],black=[['C#4',12.5],['D#4',25],['F#4',50],['G#4',62.5],['A#4',75]],box=$('v23Keyboard');if(!box)return;
 let target=x.notes||[];v23PianoProgress=0;box.innerHTML='<div class="v23-white-keys">'+white.map(n=>`<button type="button" data-v23-key="${n}" class="v23-key-white" aria-label="Play note ${n}"><span>${n.replace(/4|5/,'')}</span></button>`).join('')+'</div>'+black.map(([n,left])=>`<button type="button" data-v23-key="${n}" class="v23-key-black" style="left:${left}%" aria-label="Play note ${n}"></button>`).join('');
 function highlight(){box.querySelectorAll('[data-v23-key]').forEach(b=>b.classList.toggle('v23-target',b.dataset.v23Key===target[v23PianoProgress]));$('screen').querySelectorAll('[data-v23-noteindex]').forEach((b,i)=>{b.classList.toggle('v23-hit',i<v23PianoProgress);b.classList.toggle('v23-current',i===v23PianoProgress)})}highlight();
 box.querySelectorAll('[data-v23-key]').forEach(b=>b.onclick=()=>{const n=b.dataset.v23Key;v23Tone(n);if(n===target[v23PianoProgress]){v23PianoProgress++;$('v23PianoStatus').textContent=v23PianoProgress===target.length?'You played the whole phrase. The next note is '+target[v23PianoProgress]+'. Find it using the black keys as landmarks.'}});
 $('v23Replay').onclick=()=>{v23PianoProgress=0;highlight();$('v23PianoStatus').textContent='Start again. You can go as slowly as you like.'};
 $('v23Demo').onclick=()=>{target.forEach((n,i)=>setTimeout(()=>v23Tone(n),i*450));$('v23PianoStatus').textContent='Listen to the notes. Then try matching them.'};
}
function v23Tone(note){try{const names={C:0,D:2,E:4,F:5,G:7,A:9,B:11};let [_,name,sharp,oct]=note.match(/^([A-G])(#?)(\d)$/)||[];if(!name)return;let midi=(Number(oct)+1)*12+names[name]+(sharp?1:0),hz=440*Math.pow(2,(midi-69)/12);v23Sound=v23Sound||new(window.AudioContext||window.webkitAudioContext)();let o=v23Sound.createOscillator(),g=v23Sound.createGain();o.type='sine';o.frequency.value=hz;g.gain.setValueAtTime(.0001,v23Sound.currentTime);g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(.12,v23Sound.currentTime+.025);g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(.0001,v23Sound.currentTime+.37);o.connect(g);g.connect(v23Sound.destination);o.start();o.stop(v23Sound.currentTime+.39)}catch(e){console.warn('Audio unavailable',e.message)}}
function v23BindVisual(x){if(v23Active.subject==='calculus'){let slider=$('v23MathSlider'),draw=()=>v23DrawMath(x.visual,Number(slider.value));slider.oninput=draw;draw()}else{let slider=$('v23PhysicsSlider'),draw=()=>v23DrawPhysics(x.visual,Number(slider.value));slider.oninput=draw;draw()}}
function v23DrawMath(kind,val){const g=$('v23Graph');if(!g)return;let W=520,H=250;
 if(kind==='area'){let n=val,rects='',delta=3/n,sum=0;for(let k=0;k<n;k++){let left=k*delta,ht=2*left;sum+=ht*delta;rects+=`<rect x="${60+left*130}" y="${217-ht*28}" width="${Math.max(.1,delta*130)}" height="${ht*28}" fill="#7ba88a" opacity=".4" stroke="#285e46" stroke-width=".7"/>`};let curve='M60 217 L450 49';g.innerHTML=`<svg viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H}" role="img" aria-label="Area under the line y equals 2x from zero to three"><line x1="60" y1="217" x2="480" y2="217" stroke="#678575"/><line x1="60" y1="217" x2="60" y2="20" stroke="#678575"/>${rects}<path d="${curve}" stroke="#24543e" stroke-width="3" fill="none"/><text x="65" y="27" font-size="13" fill="#234d37">y = 2x</text><text x="445" y="236" font-size="13" fill="#234d37">3</text></svg>`;$('v23MathVal').textContent=n+' slices — estimate '+sum.toFixed(2)+' (exact area 9)';return}
 const x=val, px=t=>260+t*67,py=y=>218-y*19,curve=Array.from({length:101},(_,i)=>{let t=-3+i*.06;return `${i?'L':'M'}${px(t).toFixed(2)} ${py(t*t).toFixed(2)}`}).join(' '),m=2*x,y=x*x,tangent=`M${px(-3)} ${py(y+m*(-3-x))} L${px(3)} ${py(y+m*(3-x))}`;
 g.innerHTML=`<svg viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H}" role="img" aria-label="Parabola y equals x squared and its tangent at x ${x}"><line x1="35" y1="218" x2="485" y2="218" stroke="#879d8b"/><line x1="260" y1="8" x2="260" y2="239" stroke="#879d8b"/><path d="${curve}" stroke="#285943" stroke-width="3" fill="none"/><path d="${tangent}" stroke="#c47f4d" stroke-width="2.5" fill="none"/><circle cx="${px(x)}" cy="${py(y)}" r="6" fill="#b06128"/><text x="35" y="20" font-size="13" fill="#23513a">y=x² · slope=2x</text></svg>`;
 $('v23MathVal').textContent='x = '+x.toFixed(2)+' · tangent slope = '+m.toFixed(2);
}
function v23DrawPhysics(kind,val){let g=$('v23PhysicsFigure'),r=$('v23PhysicsReadout'),label=$('v23PhysicsLabel');if(!g)return;
 const settings={fall:['Drop height (meters)',`From ${val} meters, both objects take ~${Math.sqrt(2*val/9.81).toFixed(2)} seconds in a vacuum.`],motion:['Mass (kilograms)',`With net force 12 N and mass ${val} kg, acceleration = ${(12/val).toFixed(2)} m/s².`],energy:['Height (meters)',`A 1 kg mass at height ${val} m stores ~${(val*9.81).toFixed(1)} J of gravitational potential energy.`],circuit:['Resistance (ohms)',`At 12 V and ${val} Ω, current is ${(12/val).toFixed(2)} amperes.`],wave:['Frequency × 100 Hz',`A ${val*100} Hz tone has more cycles per second than a ${Math.max(1,val-1)*100} Hz tone.`],heat:['Temperature difference (°C)',`Difference ${val*5} °C: a larger temperature gap generally drives faster heat transfer for the same setup.`],light:['Frequency comparison',`Blue photons have higher energy than red photons because E = h × frequency.`]};
 let [lbl,text]=settings[kind]||settings.motion;label.textContent=lbl;r.textContent=text;
 if(kind==='wave'){let cyc=val*2,d=Array.from({length:140},(_,i)=>`${i?'L':'M'}${10+i*3.5} ${112-Math.sin((i/139)*cyc*Math.PI*2)*54}`).join(' ');g.innerHTML=`<svg viewBox="0 0 520 220" aria-label="Wave cycles visualization" role="img"><path d="${d}" stroke="#2d7357" stroke-width="3" fill="none"/><line x1="0" y1="112" x2="520" y2="112" stroke="#adc7af"/></svg>`;return}
 if(kind==='circuit'){g.innerHTML=`<svg viewBox="0 0 520 220" role="img" aria-label="Simple closed circuit with battery and resistor"><path d="M100 40 H390 V180 H100 Z" fill="none" stroke="#256148" stroke-width="5"/><path d="M90 80 H110 M80 94 H120" stroke="#a96537" stroke-width="4"/><rect x="362" y="86" width="55" height="40" rx="5" fill="#f5dfbb" stroke="#a87342" stroke-width="3"/><text x="230" y="25" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" fill="#28543d">12 V battery → ${val} Ω resistor</text><text x="390" y="110" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" fill="#825022">R</text></svg>`;return}
 let pct=Math.min(95,17+val*7),axis=kind==='fall'?'↓ gravity':kind==='energy'?'potential energy':kind==='motion'?'net force':kind==='heat'?'hot → cold':'light frequency';g.innerHTML=`<svg viewBox="0 0 520 220" role="img" aria-label="${axis} illustration"><rect x="55" y="185" width="425" height="5" rx="2" fill="#9db9a3"/><rect x="${kind==='motion'?50:230}" y="${195-pct*1.7}" width="${kind==='motion'?90:58}" height="${pct*1.7}" rx="7" fill="#78a789" opacity=".55"/><circle cx="${kind==='motion'?95:259}" cy="${180-pct*1.7}" r="${kind==='fall'?24:18}" fill="#2d7452"/><text x="260" y="35" text-anchor="middle" font-size="18" font-weight="700" fill="#2c6047">${axis}</text><path d="M330 75 v90" stroke="#bb743b" stroke-width="5" marker-end="url(#v23arrow)"/><defs><marker id="v23arrow" markerWidth="5" markerHeight="5" refX="5" refY="2.5" orient="auto"><path d="M0 0 L5 2.5 L0 5" fill="#bb743b"/></marker></defs></svg>`;
}

function v23VerbsHtml(){return `<details class="v23-verbs"><summary>20 verbs + the tenses you actually use</summary><p>Choose a verb, a person and a tense. See how the same idea changes. Then say it aloud.</p><div class="v23-verb-controls"><label for="v23Verb">Verb <select id="v23Verb">${V23_VERBS.map((v,i)=>`<option value="${i}">${h(v.verb)} — ${h(v.meaning)}</option>`).join('')}</select></label><label for="v23Pronoun">Person <select id="v23Pronoun"><option value="yo">yo (I)</option><option value="tu">tú (you)</option></select></label><label for="v23Tense">Tense <select id="v23Tense"><option value="present">Now</option><option value="past">Completed past</option><option value="imperfect">Habitual/background past</option><option value="future">Going to...</option><option value="subjunctive">A hope or wish</option></select></label></div><div id="v23VerbResult" class="v23-verb-result" role="status"></div><button type="button" class="v23-mini-btn" id="v23SayVerb">Hear this form</button></details>`}
function v23BindVerbs(){const verb=$('v23Verb'),who=$('v23Pronoun'),tense=$('v23Tense'),result=$('v23VerbResult');if(!verb||!who||!tense)return;let current='';
 function update(){let v=V23_VERBS[+verb.value],t=tense.value,person=who.value,key=t==='future'?null:V23_TENSES[t][person==='yo'?0:1];current=t==='future'?(person==='yo'?'voy':'vas')+' a '+v.verb:v[key];const why=V23_TENSES[t][2],example=V23_TENSES[t][3];result.innerHTML=`<span class="v23-verb-form">${h(current)}</span><p>${h(why)}</p><p class="v23-verb-example">${h(example)}</p>`;}
 for(let e of [verb,who,tense])e.onchange=update;update();$('v23SayVerb').onclick=()=>{try{window.speechSynthesis.cancel();let msg=new SpeechSynthesisUtterance(current);msg.lang='es-MX';msg.rate=.82;window.speechSynthesis.speak(msg)}catch{result.append(' — Speech playback is unavailable here.')}};
}
const __v23OldInit=v21Init;
v21Init=function(){__v23OldInit();document.title='Study Table — Full Courses · Clear First Steps';let mobile=$('v21MobileSubject');if(mobile){for(let s of ['calculus','physics']){if(!mobile.querySelector(`option[value="${s}"]`)){let o=document.createElement('option');o.value=s;o.textContent=v23Name(s);mobile.append(o)}}}
 const quick=document.querySelector('.quickbar');if(quick){let btn=document.createElement('button');btn.className='button primary';btn.id='v23StartBtn';btn.textContent='Start learning';btn.onclick=()=>v23Open('spanish');quick.insertBefore(btn,$('v22ThreeBtn'))}
 const sidebar=$('v21SidebarBtn');if(sidebar)sidebar.onclick=()=>{if(V23_TRACKS[subject])v23Open(subject);else __v23OldRoute(subject)};
 const resume=$('resumeBtn');if(resume){const older=resume.onclick;resume.onclick=()=>{let s=safeStore.get('v23:last',null);if(s?.subject&&V23_TRACKS[s.subject])v23Open(s.subject,s.index);else older()}}
 const v21Path=$('v21PathBtn');if(v21Path)v21Path.onclick=()=>{if(V23_TRACKS[subject])v23Open(subject);else __v23OldRoute(subject)};
 const help=$('helpBtn');if(help){let old=help.onclick;help.onclick=()=>{if(v23Active){v23AnswerQuestion('Make it simpler');return}old?.()}};
 document.querySelector('header .brand small').textContent='NINE SUBJECTS · COMPLETE COURSES · ONE FILE';
 $('headline').textContent='Nine subjects, including Calculus and Physics';
};

const __v23OldBackup=v21Backup;
v21Backup=function(){let data=__v23OldBackup();data.firstSteps=v23Storage();data.firstStepsLast=safeStore.get('v23:last');return data};
const __v23OldImport=importNotebook;
importNotebook=async function(file){if(!file)return;let extra=null;try{let obj=JSON.parse(await file.text());if(obj.firstSteps&&typeof obj.firstSteps==='object')extra=obj}catch{};await __v23OldImport(file);
 if(extra){const clean={};for(let [key,value] of Object.entries(extra.firstSteps)){const m=key.match(/^(spanish|piano|chess|calculus|physics):(\d+)$/);if(!m||Number(m[2])>=V23_TRACKS[m[1]].length||!['again','almost','clear'].includes(value?.level))continue;clean[key]={level:value.level,at:Number(value.at)||Date.now(),reviewAt:Number(value.reviewAt)||Date.now()}}safeStore.set('v23:lessons',clean);if(V23_TRACKS[extra.firstStepsLast?.subject])safeStore.set('v23:last',extra.firstStepsLast);}
};

function v24Norm(s){return String(s||'').normalize('NFD').replace(/[\u0300-\u036f]/g,'').toLowerCase().replace(/[¿?¡!.,;:]/g,'').replace(/\s+/g,' ').trim()}
function v24Mastery(){return safeStore.get(V24_KEY,{})||{}}
function v24Record(s,i,type){let m=v24Mastery(),key=s+':'+i,prior=m[key]||{},now=Date.now(),streak=type==='independent'?(Number(prior.streak)||0)+1:0,days=type==='independent'?[3,7,14,30][Math.min(streak-1,3)]:1;
 m[key]={...prior,[type]:now,updated:now,streak,reviewAt:now+days*86400000};safeStore.set(V24_KEY,m);v24UpdateProgress()}
function v24IsDone(s,i){return !!v24Mastery()[s+':'+i]?.independent}
function v24Due(s,i){let m=v24Mastery()[s+':'+i];return m&&Number(m.reviewAt)<=Date.now()}
function v24DueIndex(s){return V23_TRACKS[s]?.findIndex((_,i)=>v24Due(s,i))??-1}
const __v24OriginalFirst=v23First;
v23First=function(s){let due=v24DueIndex(s);if(due>=0)return due;const fresh=V23_TRACKS[s].findIndex((_,i)=>!v24Mastery()[s+':'+i]);return fresh>=0?fresh:__v24OriginalFirst(s)};
function v24UpdateProgress(){const x=v23Active;if(!x)return;let meta=$('v24MasteryMeta');if(meta){const count=V23_TRACKS[x.subject].filter((_,i)=>v24IsDone(x.subject,i)).length;meta.textContent=`${count} answered without help · ${V23_TRACKS[x.subject].filter((_,i)=>v24Due(x.subject,i)).length} due for review · ${V23_TRACKS[x.subject].length} worked lessons`;}}
function v24Speak(t){try{if(!window.speechSynthesis)throw Error('Not available');speechSynthesis.cancel();let u=new SpeechSynthesisUtterance(t);u.lang='es-MX';u.rate=.81;speechSynthesis.speak(u)}catch{}}
function v24SupportHelp(scene,type){const data=V24_SPANISH[v23Active.index];return type==='small'?data.hint:data.tip}
function v24MissionSpanish(x,index){const d=V24_SPANISH[index];return `<section class="v24-mission" id="v24SpanishMission"><div class="v24-kicker">YOUR TURN FIRST · REAL-LIFE SPANISH</div><h2>${h(d.scene)}</h2><div class="v24-roundlabel" id="v24RoundLabel">ROUND 1 OF 2 · TRY IT IN YOUR OWN WORDS</div><p class="v24-prompt" id="v24Prompt">${h(d.ask)}</p><div class="v24-entry"><label for="v24Answer" class="visually-hidden">Your Spanish answer</label><input id="v24Answer" autocomplete="off" spellcheck="false" placeholder="Type what you'd actually say"><button type="button" id="v24Check" class="v23-primary">Check it</button></div><div id="v24Response" class="v24-response" role="status" aria-live="polite">Don't worry about accent marks or punctuation. Try it before opening the answer.</div><div class="v24-tools"><button id="v24Small" type="button">Give me a small clue</button><button id="v24Model" type="button">Show a model answer</button><button id="v24Audio" type="button">Hear the Spanish</button></div><div class="v24-transfer" id="v24Transfer" hidden><strong>Good.  function mark(msg,status){feedback.textContent=msg;feedback.dataset.status=status||'neutral'}
 function target(){return round===0?d.answer:d.transferAnswer}
 function checkAnswer(){if(finished)return;const guess=v24Norm(input.value);if(!guess){mark('Give it a try. Even a partial answer is useful.','neutral');return}const ok=(round===0?d.ok:d.transferOk).some(a=>v24Norm(a)===guess);if(ok){if(round===0){firstClean=!helped&&!failed;mark('Yes — '+d.answer+'. '+advice+' You can edit and try again.','retry')}}
 function beginTransfer() {round=1;helped=false;failed=false;$('v24RoundLabel').textContent='ROUND 2 OF 2 · USE IT SOMEWHERE NEW';$('v24Prompt').textContent=d.transfer;$('v24Transfer').hidden=true;input.disabled=false;check.disabled=false;input.value='';model.textContent='Show a model answer';mark('This second situation checks whether the idea transfers.','neutral');input.focus()}
 check.onclick=checkAnswer;input.onkeydown=e=>{if(e.key==='Enter'){e.preventDefault();checkAnswer()}};small.onclick=()=>{helped=true;mark(round===0?d.hint:(index===10?'The trigger no quiero que still takes the subjunctive.':d.tip),'neutral')};model.onclick=()=>{helped=true;mark('One natural answer: '+target()+'. '+d.tip,'neutral')};audio.onclick=()=>v24Speak(target());$('v24TransferBtn').onclick=beginTransfer;
}

 let grid=[];for(const row of d.fen.split(' ')[0].split('/')){for(const ch of row){if(/[1-8]/.test(ch))for(let j=0;j<Number(ch);j++)grid.push('');else grid.push(ch)}};if(grid.length!==64)return;

   if(!selected){if(!grid[('8'-square[1])*8+'abcdefgh'.indexOf(square[0])]){setState('That square is empty.    if(selected+square===d.move){solved=true;v24Record('chess',index,hinted?'practiced':'independent');const src=root.querySelector(`[data-v24-square="${selected}"]`),dst=root.querySelector(`[data-v24-square="${square}"]`);dst.textContent=src.textContent;src.textContent='';dst.classList.add('v24-solved');src.classList.remove('v24-selected');setState('That’s the move. }

 function beginIndependent(){phase=1;step=0;misses=0;litHints=false;status.textContent='Different notes this time. The letters above show the new melody, but no keys light up. Find each note yourself.';refresh()}
 old.onclick=e=>{let b=e.target.closest('[data-v23-key]');if(!b)return;let note=b.dataset.v23Key;v23Tone(note);if(note===target()[step]){step++;if(step===target().length){if(phase===0){status.textContent='You played it! Try again.'}`}};
 $('v23Replay').onclick=()=>{phase=0;step=0;misses=0;litHints=false;status.textContent='Start slowly. The next key will light up.';refresh()};
 $('v23Demo').onclick=()=>{if(phase===1)litHints=true;target().forEach((n,i)=>setTimeout(()=>v23Tone(n),i*475));status.textContent='Listen, then try matching the notes. Showing the demo makes this a guided practice round.';refresh()};

/* A pulse cannot be learned from four untimed clicks; this small lab measures steadiness. */
function v24BeatPractice(){let main=$('screen').querySelector('.v23-main-panel'),keyboard=$('v23Keyboard');if(!main||!keyboard)return;let container=keyboard.closest('.v23-playground');if(!container)return;
 let el=document.createElement('section');el.className='v24-beat';el.innerHTML=`<div class="v24-kicker">RHYTHM LAB · HEAR THE PULSE</div><h3>Can you keep five taps evenly spaced?</h3><p>Tap at a comfortable, steady pace. What matters is the time <strong>between</strong> taps, not how fast you go. Listen for the note each time.</p><button type="button" class="v23-primary" id="v24TapBeat">Tap the beat</button><button type="button" class="v23-mini-btn" id="v24BeatReset">Try again</button><p class="v24-beat-report" id="v24BeatReport" role="status">Tap five times. We'll compare the gaps and show you your timing.</p>`;container.insertAdjacentElement('afterend',el);
 let times=[];function reset(){times=[];$('v24BeatReport').textContent='Tap five times at a comfortable, even pace. No rush.'}
 $('v24BeatReset').onclick=reset;
 $('v24TapBeat').onclick=()=>{v23Tone('C4');let now=performance.now();if(times.length&&now-times[times.length-1]>4000)times=[];times.push(now);if(times.length<5){$('v24BeatReport').textContent=times.length+' of 5 taps. Keep the intervals even.';return}let gaps=times.slice(1).map((t,i)=>t-times[i]),avg=gaps.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)/gaps.length,spread=Math.max(...gaps.map(x=>Math.abs(x-avg)))/avg,tempo=Math.round(60000/avg),stable=spread<=.2&&avg>=350&&avg<=1600;
 if(stable){v24Record('piano',2,'independent');$('v24BeatReport').textContent=`Steady! About ${tempo} beats per minute. Your largest timing deviation was ${Math.round(spread*100)}% of the average interval. That is an steady beat without help.`}else{v24Record('piano',2,'practiced');$('v24BeatReport').textContent=`About ${tempo} beats per minute, but the gaps varied by ${Math.round(spread*100)}%. Try again: count “one, two, three, four, five” out loud and tap on each count.`}times=[];
 };
}

function v24FallPractice(){const main=$('screen').querySelector('.v23-main-panel'),hook=main?.querySelector('.v23-hook');if(!hook)return;let p=document.createElement('section');p.className='v24-mission';p.id='v24FallMission';p.innerHTML=`<div class="v24-kicker">PREDICT THE EXPERIMENT</div><h2>Two balls, two different masses.</h2><p>Drop both from the same height in a vacuum.  let firstClean=false,helped=false,missed=false,finished=false;const feedback=$('v24FallFeedback');let msg=(t,status='neutral')=>{feedback.textContent=t;feedback.dataset.status=status};

In a vacuum, both accelerate at about 9.8 m/s².','right');p.querySelector('#v24FallTransfer').hidden=false;}else{missed=true;msg('Consider what happens without air resistance. Does greater mass also mean greater resistance to acceleration?','retry')}});
 p.querySelectorAll('[data-height]').forEach(btn=>btn.onclick=()=>{if(finished)return;let right=btn.dataset.height==='longer';if(right){finished=true;const success=firstClean&&!helped;v24Record('physics',0,success?'independent':'practiced');msg(success?'You predicted both effects without help. Try another time without hints to check recall.','right');p.querySelectorAll('button[data-height],button[data-fall]').forEach(b=>b.disabled=true)}else{helped=true;msg('A longer fall means gravity has farther to accelerate the ball. Try “longer.”','retry')}});
 p.querySelector('#v24FallHint').onclick=()=>{helped=true;msg('In a vacuum, air resistance is absent. Gravitational force and inertia both scale with mass. The time depends on the drop height and gravitational acceleration, not the mass.','neutral')};
 v24WrapDetails(main.querySelector('.v23-theidea'),'Why mass cancels out · the reasoning');v24WrapDetails(main.querySelector('.v23-check'),'Optional: another question');
}

/* Study Table V25 — explicit model answers, on demand, in every current practice mode. */
(function(){
'use strict';
function el(tag,cls,txt){const n=document.createElement(tag);if(cls)n.className=cls;if(txt)n.textContent=txt;return n}
function revealBox(parent,id,buttonText){
  if(!parent)return null;
  let wrap=parent.querySelector('#'+id);
  if(!wrap){wrap=el('div','v25-reveal-wrap');wrap.id=id;
    const button=el('button','v25-reveal-button',buttonText||'Show answer + why');button.type='button';button.setAttribute('aria-expanded','false');
    const answer=el('div','v25-reveal-content');answer.hidden=true;answer.setAttribute('role','status');
    button.addEventListener('click',()=>{const opening=answer.hidden;answer.hidden=!opening;button.setAttribute('aria-expanded',String(opening));if(opening&&typeof wrap.beforeReveal==='function')wrap.beforeReveal();});
    wrap.append(button,answer);parent.appendChild(wrap);
  }
  return {wrap,button:wrap.firstElementChild,body:wrap.lastElementChild};
}
function sectionAnswer(parent,id,title,answer,why,extra=''){
 const widget=revealBox(parent,id,'Show answer + why');if(!widget)return;
 widget.wrap.beforeReveal=()=>{widget.body.innerHTML='<strong>'+h(title)+'</strong><p class="v25-model">'+h(answer)+'</p><p>'+h(why)+'</p>'+(extra?'<p class="v25-note">'+h(extra)+'</p>':'');};
}

 // The original conceptual quiz already includes a verified correct choice; make its answer button explicit.

 if(s==='spanish'){

         'calculus:0':['48 ÷ 12 = 4 meters per second.','75 ÷ 15 = 5 meters per second.'],
         'calculus:1':['For y = x², the derivative is 2x. At x = 2, slope = 4.','For y = x², derivative 2x. At x = −1, slope = −2.'],
         'physics:1':['Velocity change = 16 − 4 = 12 m/s; 12 ÷ 3 = 4 m/s².','Velocity change = 14 − 2 = 12 m/s; 12 ÷ 4 = 3 m/s².'],

       };
       ex.onclick=()=>{if(core)core();const phase=String($('v24MathRound')?.textContent||'').includes('SECOND')?1:0;const reasoning=worked[s+':'+i]?.[phase];if(reasoning){const f=$('v24MathFeedback');f.textContent='Model solution: '+reasoning;f.dataset.status='neutral'}};
     }

 }
 if(s==='chess'){

       widget.body.innerHTML='<strong>Correct move</strong><p class="v25-model">'+h(format)+'</p><p>'+h(d.why)+'</p><p class="v25-note">The highlighted squares show the answer. You can still make the move yourself.</p>';
     };
   }
 }
 if(s==='piano'){
   const piano=$('v24PianoMission'),keyboard=$('v23Keyboard');if(piano&&keyboard){
     let tools=piano.querySelector('.v25-piano-tools');if(!tools){tools=el('div','v25-piano-tools');piano.appendChild(tools)}
     const widget=revealBox(tools,'v25PianoReveal','Show the exact notes + how to play');
     widget.wrap.beforeReveal=()=>{
       // Replay demo marks the unlit round as assisted in the original lesson state.
       const demo=$('v23Demo');if(demo)demo.click();

       const phase=$('v24PianoRound')?.textContent||'';
       widget.body.innerHTML='<strong>'+(phase.includes('ROUND 2')?'New pattern':'Guided melody')+'</strong><p class="v25-model">'+h(seq)+'</p><p>Read each note left to right, then press the white key with that letter. C is immediately left of the pair of black keys. Each note plays once, in the displayed order.</p><p class="v25-note">The demonstration also plays the melody so you can hear what the answer should sound like.</p>';
     };
     // A later round has a different pattern; do not leave the earlier answer on screen.
     const response=$('v23PianoStatus');if(response){const observer=new MutationObserver(()=>{const label=$('v24PianoRound')?.textContent||'';if(widget.wrap.dataset.round!==label){widget.wrap.dataset.round=label;widget.body.hidden=true;widget.button.setAttribute('aria-expanded','false')}});observer.observe($('v24PianoRound'),{childList:true,subtree:true});widget.wrap.dataset.round=$('v24PianoRound')?.textContent||'';}
   }
 }
 if(s==='piano'&&i===2){
   const beat=$('v24BeatReport')?.closest('.v24-beat');if(beat){
     sectionAnswer(beat,'v25BeatReveal','What a correct answer sounds like','Five evenly spaced taps: for example, one tap every 600 milliseconds (100 BPM).','The gaps should be nearly equal. You can choose a different comfortable speed; accuracy means consistency, not copying 100 BPM.','Count aloud “1, 2, 3, 4, 5” and tap once on every number.');
   }
 }
 if(s==='physics'&&i===0){
   const lesson=$('v24FallMission');if(lesson){
     const tools=lesson.querySelector('.v24-tools');
     const widget=revealBox(tools,'v25FallReveal','Show both answers + the physics');
     widget.wrap.beforeReveal=()=>{
       const b=$('v24FallHint');if(b)b.click();
       widget.body.innerHTML='<strong>Question 1 — which ball lands first?</strong><p class="v25-model">They arrive together (in a vacuum).</p><p>Acceleration from gravity is the same for both masses when air resistance is absent.</p><strong>Question 2 — what happens from a higher platform?</strong><p class="v25-model">The fall takes longer.</p><p>A greater drop distance takes more time at the same gravitational acceleration.</p>';
       const second=$('v24FallTransfer');if(second)second.hidden=false;
     };
   }
 }
};
const originalSessionRender=v22RenderSession;
v22RenderSession=function(){originalSessionRender();

/* A stable answer action for ALL embedded archive pages, independent of inner-page scrolling. */
(function(){
'use strict';
const shell=document.createElement('div');shell.id='v25UniversalReveal';shell.hidden=true;
shell.innerHTML='<section id="v25UniversalAnswer" class="v25-outer-answer" hidden role="region" aria-label="Correct answer and explanation"><button type="button" id="v25UniversalClose" aria-label="Close answer">✕</button><h3>Answer + explanation</h3><div id="v25UniversalContent"></div></section><button type="button" id="v25UniversalShow" aria-expanded="false">Show answer + why</button>';
document.body.appendChild(shell);
function close(){const pane=$('v25UniversalAnswer');pane.hidden=true;$('v25UniversalShow').setAttribute('aria-expanded','false')}
$('v25UniversalClose').onclick=close;
window.addEventListener('message',e=>{if(e.source===$('frame')?.contentWindow&&e.data?.type==='v25-question-changed'&&e.data?.page===splitPath(activePath))close()});
function update(){const frame=$('frame'),valid=!!frame&&!!activePath&&/\.html(?:[?#]|$)/i.test(activePath)&&!v23Active&&!v22Session;
 shell.hidden=!valid;if(!valid)close()}
$('v25UniversalShow').onclick=()=>{
 const pane=$('v25UniversalAnswer');if(!pane.hidden){close();return}
 const frame=$('frame');const doc=frame?.contentDocument;
 const btn=doc?.getElementById('v25ArchiveToggle');
 if(!btn){$('v25UniversalContent').textContent='This page is still loading or has no verified answer key.';pane.hidden=false;return}
 const embeddedPane=doc.getElementById('v25ArchivedAnswer');
 if(embeddedPane?.getAttribute('aria-hidden')==='false')btn.click();
 btn.click();
 const src=doc.getElementById('v25ArchiveContent');
 const content=$('v25UniversalContent');content.textContent=src?.innerText?.trim()||'Open the lesson to see its source-provided answer.';
 pane.hidden=false;$('v25UniversalShow').setAttribute('aria-expanded','true');
};
// The page swaps its viewer content when opening, closing or changing courses.
const observer=new MutationObserver(update);observer.observe($('screen'),{childList:true,subtree:false});
const oldGo=go;go=function(path,opts={}){close();return oldGo(path,opts)};
const oldOpen=v23Open;v23Open=function(s,i=null){close();return oldOpen(s,i)};
const oldHome=showHome;showHome=function(){close();return oldHome()};
const oldSession=v22Begin;v22Begin=function(mode='easy',sub='all'){close();return oldSession(mode,sub)};
update();
})();

What should breathing generally do?","answer":"Speed up to remove CO₂.","why":"Ventilation rises to eliminate CO₂ and help maintain blood pH.
