These are the same spacing as C–E–G, moved up.","title":"A major chord is a shape","source":"aristotle"}],"v15/chess-from-zero/index.html":[{"prompt":"Your rook is on d4, the board otherwise empty. Which move is legal?","answer":"d7","why":"The rook stays on a file or a rank. d4 to d7 is straight up the d-file; f7 and a1 are diagonals.","title":"The rook","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"A bishop on c1 has an empty board. Which square lies on its diagonal?","answer":"f4","why":"From c1, moving three files right and three ranks up reaches f4. The other choices break the diagonal.","title":"The bishop","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"A knight is on e4. Which square can it reach in one move?","answer":"f6","why":"e4 to f6 moves one file right and two ranks up. The other choices are not knight moves.","title":"The knight","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"A king on e4 is not in check. Which square is exactly one king step away?","answer":"f5","why":"The king can move one square in any direction, assuming the destination is not attacked. f5 is one file and one rank away.","title":"The king","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"A white pawn is on e4 and there are no pieces nearby. Where may it move?","answer":"e5","why":"From e4 a white pawn may advance one square to e5 if it is clear. It may only capture on f5, and e6 is not a legal two-square move from e4.","title":"The pawn","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"Your queen is on d4. Which move is NOT legal on an otherwise empty board?","answer":"e6","why":"e6 changes file by one and rank by two: neither a diagonal nor a straight line. h8 is diagonal and d8 is vertical.","title":"The queen","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"Your rook starts on b2. Which move is legal on an empty board?","answer":"g2","why":"b2 to g2 stays on the second rank. Both other squares require a diagonal.","title":"Second rook route","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"Your bishop is on f1. Which destination stays on its diagonal?","answer":"c4","why":"f1 to c4 moves three files left and three ranks up. A bishop cannot move straight up to f5.","title":"Bishop color","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"A knight starts on b1. Which square can it jump to?","answer":"c3","why":"b1 to c3 is one file right and two ranks up. d3 is two files and two ranks; b3 is straight up.","title":"Knight takes a leap","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"Your queen is on a4 and all squares are free. Which square can she reach?","answer":"d7","why":"a4 to d7 moves three files and three ranks. e6 and b7 are not on the same rank, file or diagonal.","title":"Queen’s diagonal","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"A king stands on c3 and no destination is attacked. Which move is legal?","answer":"b4","why":"b4 is one step diagonally away. e3 moves two files, and a2 moves two files and one rank.","title":"Kings stay nearby","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"A white pawn stands on e2. The squares e3 and e4 are free. Which move is legal?","answer":"e4","why":"A pawn can advance two squares from its starting rank if both squares are clear. It cannot jump to e5 or capture on d3 without an enemy piece.","title":"Pawn’s first push","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"A white pawn stands on d4. Where can it capture an enemy piece?","answer":"e5","why":"A white pawn captures one rank forward and one file across. From d4, e5 is a capture square; d5 is a non-capturing push.","title":"Pawn captures","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"Your knight begins on g1. Which move can it make?","answer":"f3","why":"g1 to f3 is one file left and two ranks up. The other squares are not a knight’s L-shaped move.","title":"A surprise knight move","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"You can castle kingside. What changes on the board?","answer":"The king moves two files toward the rook; the rook lands next to it.","why":"In white kingside castling, the king goes e1–g1 and the rook h1–f1, subject to the castling conditions.","title":"Castling purpose","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"Your king is in check and you can capture an enemy pawn elsewhere. What must you do?","answer":"Make a legal move that gets your king out of check.","why":"A move is legal only if your king is no longer in check afterward. A counter-check is fine only if it also ends your check.","title":"What is check?","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"You can take the enemy queen, but your own queen will then be captured. What should you check first?","answer":"The material balance and tactical consequences after the exchange.","why":"Calculate the sequence. Taking a queen can still be bad if the recapture or position costs you more.","title":"Free queen?","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"It is your turn. Your king is safe, but you have no legal move. Result?","answer":"Draw by stalemate.","why":"Stalemate is a draw: no legal moves while not in check. Checkmate requires the king to be in check.","title":"Checkmate vs. stalemate","source":"quick-practice"},{"prompt":"Which square can a knight on d4 reach in one move?","answer":"f5","why":"d4 → f5 goes two files to the right and one rank up. d6 moves straight and f4 moves only sideways.","title":"The knight does not walk there","source":"aristotle"},{"prompt":"Which square can the bishop on c1 reach on an empty board?","answer":"h6","why":"c1 → h6 is five squares right and five up: a diagonal. It cannot change square colour.","title":"A bishop is trapped by its colour","source":"aristotle"},{"prompt":"Your bishop is the only piece blocking a rook from attacking your king. Can the bishop simply move away?","answer":"No, not if it exposes your king to check.","why":"Every legal move must leave your own king safe. Movement rules are necessary, but king safety is the final test.","title":"A pinned piece can look free","source":"aristotle"},{"prompt":"Your knight can attack both the queen and rook next move. Why can this be powerful?","answer":"The opponent may only save one piece.","why":"On the next turn the opponent usually has time to answer only one threat. But check whether the knight can be captured first.","title":"A fork makes one move do two jobs","source":"aristotle"},{"prompt":"Which piece makes an L-shaped jump?","answer":"Knight","why":"The knight hops two squares, then one sideways.","source":"chess-quiz"},{"prompt":"Which piece may jump OVER other pieces?","answer":"Knight","why":"Only the knight can jump.","source":"chess-quiz"},{"prompt":"How does a pawn capture?","answer":"Diagonally forward","why":"A pawn walks straight, but captures diagonally forward.","source":"chess-quiz"},{"prompt":"Which piece moves only diagonally?","answer":"Bishop","why":"Bishops slide along diagonals.","source":"chess-quiz"},{"prompt":"Which piece moves in straight lines only?","answer":"Rook","why":"A rook moves along rows and columns.","source":"chess-quiz"},{"prompt":"Which piece combines a rook and a bishop?","answer":"Queen","why":"The queen moves straight and diagonally.","source":"chess-quiz"},{"prompt":"How far does a king normally move?","answer":"One square","why":"The king moves one square in any direction, unless it castles.","source":"chess-quiz"},{"prompt":"What happens when your king is in check?","answer":"You must end the check","why":"You must make a legal move that removes the check.","source":"chess-quiz"},{"prompt":"What wins a game of chess?","answer":"Checkmate","why":"Checkmate: a king is attacked with no legal escape.","source":"chess-quiz"},{"prompt":"Which piece is worth roughly 9 points?","answer":"Queen","why":"Queen ~9; rook ~5; bishop/knight ~3; pawn ~1.","source":"chess-quiz"},{"prompt":"Where does the white queen start?","answer":"d1","why":"Queen on her own color: white queen d1, black queen d8.","source":"chess-quiz"},{"prompt":"Which three words help prevent blunders?","answer":"Danger, Free, Safe","why":"DANGER: what threatens me? FREE: what can I take? SAFE: can they punish my move?","source":"chess-quiz"}],"v15/body-school/clinic.html":[{"prompt":"Why might oxygen delivery still be reduced?","answer":"Less hemoglobin can mean less oxygen carried, even when much of the available hemoglobin is saturated.","why":"Oxygen saturation measures the fraction of hemoglobin binding sites occupied, not the amount of hemoglobin. Delivery also depends on cardiac output and tissue extraction.","title":"Oxygen isn't one number","source":"clinic"},{"prompt":"What is the main useful response?","answer":"The kidneys can conserve water, aided by increased antidiuretic hormone signaling.","why":"Volume and osmolality sensors influence thirst and kidney water handling. ADH increases collecting-duct water reabsorption; other responses, including the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system, also help conserve salt and volume.","title":"The disappearing water","source":"clinic"},{"prompt":"Why does a small change in airway radius matter?","answer":"In a simplified laminar-flow tube, resistance rises sharply as radius decreases.","why":"For ideal laminar flow in a rigid circular tube, resistance varies approximately with 1/r⁴ (Poiseuille's law). Real lungs are branching, flexible and sometimes turbulent, so this is a teaching analogy.","title":"Why narrow airways matter","source":"clinic"},{"prompt":"How can breathing partly compensate?","answer":"Blowing off more CO₂ can lower carbonic acid and partly offset the fall in pH.","why":"Reducing arterial CO₂ shifts the bicarbonate buffer equilibrium and helps raise pH toward normal. This is compensation, not necessarily correction of the underlying metabolic process.","title":"The breath that fights acid","source":"clinic"},{"prompt":"Which calculation captures the difference?","answer":"Cardiac output is 4.9 L/min for A and 3.5 L/min for B.","why":"Heart rate × stroke volume gives flow per minute. 70 × 70 = 4,900 mL/min, or 4.9 L/min. 70 × 50 = 3,500 mL/min. These fictional values are for learning, not diagnosis.","title":"Same pulse, different blood flow","source":"clinic"},{"prompt":"What happens to pressure in this model?","answer":"It doubles.","why":"The same force divided by half the area produces twice the pressure. A rigid piston is only a mechanical analogy, not a complete model of blood pressure.","title":"Pressure is not force","source":"clinic"},{"prompt":"What is the final concentration?","answer":"5 mmol/L.","why":"Concentration equals solute amount divided by total solution volume. Here 10 mmol ÷ 2 L = 5 mmol/L.","title":"Water changes the denominator","source":"clinic"},{"prompt":"How many units remain after two half-lives?","answer":"20: 80 → 40 → 20.","why":"Two half-lives mean multiply by (1/2) twice. 80 × (1/2)² = 20. Real pharmacokinetics can differ and should not be inferred from this exercise.","title":"Half-life is repeated halving","source":"clinic"},{"prompt":"How likely is genotype aa for any one child?","answer":"25% (one combination out of four).","why":"Each parent independently passes A or a with probability one-half, so P(aa)=1/2 × 1/2=1/4. Each pregnancy has a new probability.","title":"Two carriers, four possibilities","source":"clinic"},{"prompt":"Which explanation fits the model?","answer":"Many active sites are occupied, so more substrate adds less speed.","why":"In a simple Michaelis–Menten model, reaction rate approaches a maximum as substrate rises. Not every real enzyme obeys this exact model.","title":"When enzymes get crowded","source":"clinic"}]};

They are not proof that every advanced skill is fully taught or assessed. “Explored” is not mastery.</p></section>`}

You can use quiero in casual settings, but quisiera sounds softer.',['me gustaria un cafe por favor','un cafe por favor'],['me gustaria un vaso de agua']);

Could you say it again?”','No entiendo. ¿Puedes decirlo otra vez?','Puedes / podrías + infinitive. Más despacio = more slowly.','With poder + infinitive you can make a request without changing the second verb.',['podrias repetir mas despacio','puedes repetirlo mas despacio','lo podrias repetir mas despacio'],['no entiendo puedes repetirlo','no entiendo puedes repetirlo otra vez','no entiendo lo puedes decir otra vez']);
v27S('Everyday conversation','Say where you are','Someone calls to ask where you are.','Say: “I’m at home right now.”','Estoy en casa ahora.','Say: “My friend is at the restaurant.”','Mi amigo está en el restaurante.','Location uses estar. Estoy = I am; está = he/she is.','Ser identifies; estar locates or describes a current condition.',['ahora estoy en casa','estoy en mi casa ahora'],['mi amiga esta en el restaurante','mi amigo esta en el restaurant','mi amiga esta en el restaurant']);
v27S('Everyday conversation','Explain how you feel','Someone asks how your day is going.','Say: “I’m tired but happy.”','Estoy cansado pero contento.','Say: “Today I’m nervous.”','Hoy estoy nervioso.','Temporary feelings typically use estar. Adapt the adjective ending when needed.','Estoy is the present yo form of estar. Adjectives often agree with the speaker.',['estoy cansada pero contenta','estoy cansado pero feliz','estoy cansada pero feliz'],['hoy estoy nerviosa','estoy nervioso hoy','estoy nerviosa hoy']);
v27S('Everyday conversation','Ask the right question','A friend says they have plans.','Ask: “What are you doing tomorrow?”','¿Qué haces mañana?','Ask: “Where are we going?”','¿Adónde vamos?','Qué asks what; adónde asks to where.','Spanish uses question words with accents, but this app accepts typing without them.',['que vas a hacer manana','que estas haciendo manana'],['a donde vamos','donde vamos']);
v27S('Essential verbs','Want, need, can','You are explaining what you can do.','Say: “I need to work, but I want to rest.”','Necesito trabajar, pero quiero descansar.','Say: “I can help you tomorrow.”','Puedo ayudarte mañana.','Necesito / quiero / puedo + unchanged infinitive.','The conjugated first verb carries person and tense; the second remains infinitive.',['tengo que trabajar pero quiero descansar'],['te puedo ayudar manana','manana puedo ayudarte','manana te puedo ayudar']);
v27S('Essential verbs','Have to versus have','You need to leave a meeting.','Say: “I have to go now.”','Tengo que irme ahora.','Say: “I have two meetings today.”','Tengo dos reuniones hoy.','Tengo que + infinitive means obligation; tengo alone means possession.','The little que is important: tengo que irme means I must leave.',['me tengo que ir ahora','tengo que salir ahora'],['hoy tengo dos reuniones']);
v27S('Essential verbs','Talking about routines','Someone asks about your typical mornings.','Say: “I work in the morning.”','Trabajo por la mañana.','Say: “She studies Spanish every day.”','Ella estudia español todos los días.','Regular -ar verbs: yo -o, ella -a.','The present tense can describe routines, not just this instant.',['trabajo en la manana','por la manana trabajo'],['estudia espanol todos los dias','ella estudia espanol cada dia']);
v27S('Essential verbs','There is / there are','You are finding something nearby.','Say: “There is a restaurant near here.”','Hay un restaurante cerca de aquí.','Say: “There are three chairs in the room.”','Hay tres sillas en la habitación.','Hay works with both singular and plural.','Spanish uses hay for existence, not está/están, which locate something already identified.',['hay un restaurant cerca de aqui'],['hay tres sillas en el cuarto','hay tres sillas en la sala']);
v27S('Essential verbs','Like versus want','A friend asks about your tastes.','Say: “I like coffee, but I want tea.”','Me gusta el café, pero quiero té.','Say: “We like these books.”','Nos gustan estos libros.','Gusta agrees with the thing liked: gustan when that thing is plural.','Me gusta literally follows a pattern like “coffee is pleasing to me”; plural subjects need gustan.',['me gusta cafe pero quiero te'],['nos gustan los libros','a nosotros nos gustan estos libros']);
v27S('Past tense','A completed event','Tell a friend about yesterday.','Say: “Yesterday I called my friend.”','Ayer llamé a mi amigo.','Say: “I worked until six.”','Trabajé hasta las seis.','Completed -ar actions with yo end in -é.','Preterite puts a boundary around an action: it happened and finished.',['ayer llame a mi amiga','llame a mi amigo ayer','llame a mi amiga ayer'],['yo trabaje hasta las seis']);
v27S('Past tense','An irregular trip','You returned from somewhere.','Say: “Yesterday I went to the market.”','Ayer fui al mercado.','Say: “We went to the beach.”','Fuimos a la playa.','Ir has a special past form: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos.','Fui can mean I went or I was in the preterite; context resolves it.',['fui al mercado ayer'],['nosotros fuimos a la playa']);
v27S('Past tense','Background and habits','You are describing your childhood.','Say: “When I was little, I lived in Chicago.”','Cuando era pequeño, vivía en Chicago.','Say: “I used to read at night.”','Leía por la noche.','Imperfect describes habits and ongoing background: era, vivía, leía.','The imperfect has no sharp endpoint. It sets a scene or describes what used to happen.',['cuando era pequeno vivia en chicago','cuando era nina vivia en chicago','cuando era nino vivia en chicago','cuando era pequena vivia en chicago'],['antes leia por la noche','leia de noche']);
v27S('Past tense','Event versus background','A phone call interrupted your activity.','Say: “I was eating when you called.”','Estaba comiendo cuando llamaste.','Say: “I was studying when she arrived.”','Estaba estudiando cuando llegó.','Estaba + -ando/-iendo sets the scene; llamaste/llegó interrupts it.','The imperfect progressive is ongoing background; the preterite is the completed interrupting event.',['cuando llamaste estaba comiendo'],['cuando llego estaba estudiando']);
v27S('Past tense','Choosing the past','Two things happened yesterday.','Say: “I had dinner and then I left.”','Cené y después me fui.','Say: “It was raining when I left.”','Llovía cuando salí.','Completed sequence: preterite. Ongoing weather: imperfect.','Finished actions advance the story; imperfect gives the backdrop.',['cene y luego me fui','comi y despues me fui'],['cuando sali llovia','estaba lloviendo cuando sali']);
v27S('Making plans','A near-future plan','You are explaining tomorrow’s plans.','Say: “I’m going to study tonight.”','Voy a estudiar esta noche.','Say: “We’re going to eat at eight.”','Vamos a comer a las ocho.','Ir + a + infinitive is a versatile future construction.','Voy / vamos expresses the person; estudiar / comer remains unchanged.',['esta noche voy a estudiar'],['a las ocho vamos a comer']);
v27S('Making plans','The future tense','You make a prediction.','Say: “Tomorrow I’ll call you.”','Te llamaré mañana.','Say: “We will arrive early.”','Llegaremos temprano.','Keep the infinitive and add -é or -emos.','Simple future works for predictions and promises, and for guesses about the present.',['manana te llamare','te voy a llamar manana'],['vamos a llegar temprano']);
v27S('Making plans','The conditional','Discuss an imagined situation.','Say: “I would travel if I had time.”','Viajaría si tuviera tiempo.','Say: “I would buy it if it were cheaper.”','Lo compraría si fuera más barato.','Conditional -ía pairs naturally with si + imperfect subjunctive.','Hypothetical “would” is conditional, while the if-clause uses past subjunctive for an unreal present.',['si tuviera tiempo viajaria'],['si fuera mas barato lo compraria']);
v27S('Making plans','Polite requests','You want someone to send a document.','Say: “Could you send me the document?”','¿Me podrías enviar el documento?','Say: “Could you help us?”','¿Nos podrías ayudar?','Me/nos can appear before podrías or attach to the second verb.','Pronoun position is flexible with two verbs: me podrías enviar = podrías enviarme.',['podrias enviarme el documento','podrias mandarme el documento','me podrias mandar el documento'],['podrias ayudarnos','nos podria ayudar','podria ayudarnos']);
v27S('Pronouns and everyday grammar','Say it without repeating nouns','You saw the book and you purchased it.','Say: “I bought it yesterday.” (referring to a book)','Lo compré ayer.','Say: “I saw her this morning.”','La vi esta mañana.','Lo replaces masculine direct object; la can replace feminine direct object.','Object pronouns usually appear before a single conjugated verb.',['ayer lo compre'],['la vi hoy por la manana','esta manana la vi']);
v27S('Pronouns and everyday grammar','Give something to someone','You are sending someone a message.','Say: “I sent him a message.”','Le envié un mensaje.','Say: “I gave it to her.”','Se lo di.','Le becomes se when immediately followed by lo/la/los/las.','The transformation avoids le lo: the standard combination is se lo.',['le mande un mensaje'],['yo se lo di']);
v27S('Pronouns and everyday grammar','Reflexive routines','Describe getting ready.','Say: “I wake up at seven.”','Me despierto a las siete.','Say: “I’m going to get up early.”','Voy a levantarme temprano.','Reflexive me belongs with the verb and can attach to an infinitive.','Me despierto and voy a levantarme both refer the action back to the speaker.',['a las siete me despierto'],['me voy a levantar temprano']);
v27S('Pronouns and everyday grammar','Por versus para','You explain why you did something.','Say: “I did it for you.”','Lo hice por ti.','Say: “This gift is for you.”','Este regalo es para ti.','Por often explains cause, exchange or on someone’s behalf; para marks recipient or purpose.','Por ti can mean because of you/on your behalf; para ti identifies who receives the gift.',['hice esto por ti'],['el regalo es para ti']);
v27S('Subjunctive you can use','Ask someone to do something','You want your friend to call.','Say: “I want you to call me tomorrow.”','Quiero que me llames mañana.','Say: “I hope she comes.”','Espero que venga.','Different subject after want/hope + que → subjunctive.','Quiero que expresses a desired action, not a fact. Llames is subjunctive tú.',['quiero que me llames manana por favor'],['espero que ella venga']);
v27S('Subjunctive you can use','Express doubt','You are not sure someone has time.','Say: “I doubt he has time.”','Dudo que tenga tiempo.','Say: “I don’t think they are here.”','No creo que estén aquí.','Dudo que / no creo que often signal subjunctive.','Tenga / estén describe a doubted or negated proposition rather than asserting it.',['dudo que el tenga tiempo'],['no creo que esten aca']);
v27S('Subjunctive you can use','Possibility versus certainty','You are comparing what you know with what is possible.','Say: “I know that she is here.”','Sé que está aquí.','Say: “It’s possible that she is here.”','Es posible que esté aquí.','Certain assertion → está; possibility after que → esté.','A change in certainty changes the mood in these constructions.',['se que ella esta aqui'],['es posible que ella este aqui']);
v27S('Subjunctive you can use','After “when”','Your plans depend on the future.','Say: “I’ll call you when I arrive.”','Te llamaré cuando llegue.','Say: “We will eat when he comes.”','Comeremos cuando venga.','Cuando + future event uses present subjunctive.','Llegue / venga does not mean past here; it marks an anticipated event.',['cuando llegue te llamare','te voy a llamar cuando llegue'],['vamos a comer cuando venga']);
v27S('Connecting ideas','Explain a reason','You are declining an invitation.','Say: “I can’t go because I have to work.”','No puedo ir porque tengo que trabajar.','Say: “Although I’m tired, I want to go.”','Aunque estoy cansado, quiero ir.','Porque gives the reason; aunque creates contrast.','Connectors let you make meaningful longer sentences instead of isolated fragments.',['porque tengo que trabajar no puedo ir'],['aunque estoy cansada quiero ir']);
v27S('Connecting ideas','Tell a short story','You are giving an update.','Say: “Yesterday I went to the store, but it was closed.”','Ayer fui a la tienda, pero estaba cerrada.','Say: “I called her because I needed help.”','La llamé porque necesitaba ayuda.','Fui/llamé = completed event; estaba/necesitaba = background state.','Combining preterite and imperfect makes your story clearer.',['fui a la tienda ayer pero estaba cerrada'],['le llame porque necesitaba ayuda']);
v27S('Connecting ideas','An opinion with nuance','You’re deciding what to do.','Say: “I think it’s a good idea, but I’m not sure.”','Creo que es una buena idea, pero no estoy seguro.','Say: “I don’t think it’s a good idea.”','No creo que sea una buena idea.','Creo que asserts; no creo que tends to trigger subjunctive.','The switch from es to sea conveys changed stance toward the proposition.',['creo que es buena idea pero no estoy segura','creo que es buena idea pero no estoy seguro'],['no pienso que sea una buena idea']);
function v27P(unit,title,context,notes,transfer,clue,why){V27_DATA.piano.push({unit,title,context,question:'Play the notes shown below in order.',notes,transferNotes:transfer,clue,why,type:'piano'})}
v27P('Find your way','Where C lives','Find C: it is the white key immediately to the LEFT of a group of two black keys.',['C4','D4','C4'],['C4','E4','C4'],'C sits before two black keys. D is the next white key; E follows D.','Your first map: C–D–E, three neighboring white keys.');
v27P('Find your way','Three fingers','Right hand: thumb on C, pointer on D, middle on E.',['C4','D4','E4','D4','C4'],['E4','D4','C4'],'Use 1–2–3–2–1 for C D E D C.','A short rising-and-falling phrase builds finger control and location.');
v27P('Find your way','Meet F and G','Move farther to the right.',['C4','D4','E4','F4','G4'],['G4','F4','E4','D4','C4'],'C D E are before the pair of black keys. F and G come after.','A five-note range is enough to play a surprising number of songs.');
v27P('Find your way','One musical question','End on C to make the little phrase feel finished.',['C4','E4','G4','E4','C4'],['C4','D4','G4','C4'],'Start and finish on C. Think of the middle notes as a trip away from home.','The tonic note often gives a phrase a sense of arrival.');
v27P('Melodies','Mary, first phrase','Try a recognizable melody. No perfect timing required yet.',['E4','D4','C4','D4','E4','E4','E4'],['D4','D4','D4','E4','G4','G4'],'Start on E: down to D, down to C, then walk back up.','Melodies are ordered pitches with rhythm; start by getting the pitch order right.');
v27P('Melodies','Mary, second phrase','Add the response and finish.',['D4','D4','D4','E4','G4','G4'],['E4','D4','C4','D4','E4','E4','E4'],'The second phrase begins D D D.','Recognizing a repeated sequence makes longer songs easier to remember.');
v27P('Melodies','Ode to Joy','Play the first phrase from Beethoven’s tune.',['E4','E4','F4','G4','G4','F4','E4','D4'],['C4','C4','D4','E4','E4','D4','D4'],'E E F G. The melody climbs one step, then comes down.','An actual piece can be learned a phrase at a time instead of overwhelming you.');
v27P('Melodies','Twinkle','The big jump in a familiar song.',['C4','C4','G4','G4','A4','A4','G4'],['F4','F4','E4','E4','D4','D4','C4'],'C to G is a fifth: count five letter names C D E F G.','Intervals describe the distance between notes; the leap C→G is a perfect fifth.');
v27P('Keys and sharps','Find the black keys','Sharps are a half step above the letter.',['C4','C#4','D4','D#4','E4'],['F4','F#4','G4','G#4','A4'],'C# is the black key between C and D. E to F has no black key.','Chromatic notes are separated by semitones; most pairs of white keys have a black key between.');
v27P('Keys and sharps','A minor-sounding fragment','Play this short minor gesture.',['A4','C5','B4','A4'],['A4','B4','C5','A4'],'A4 is just after G4. C5 is the next C up.','Minor melodies can sound different because of their interval pattern.');
v27P('Hands and harmony','Lower C for the left hand','The lower octave is to the left.',['C3','G3','C4'],['C3','E3','G3','C4'],'Look for the C before two black keys on the left side of the keyboard.','A bass note makes a melody sound supported and helps your left hand navigate.');
v27P('Hands and harmony','Left-right conversation','The lower notes answer the upper notes.',['C3','G3','C4','E4','G4'],['F3','C4','F4','A4'],'The 3 means a lower octave; the 4 means middle C and above.','Alternating hands is a first step toward coordinated playing. This exercise checks order, not simultaneous fingering.');
v27P('Hands and harmony','The sound of a major chord','Play the notes of C major as an arpeggio (one after another).',['C4','E4','G4','C5'],['C5','G4','E4','C4'],'C, skip D, E, skip F, G. This stacks thirds.','C–E–G forms a major triad. Playing notes in succession is an arpeggio.');
v27P('Hands and harmony','The sound of a minor chord','Change just one chord tone.',['A3','C4','E4','A4'],['A4','E4','C4','A3'],'A minor = A C E. Start with A3, the lower A.','A–C–E is A minor; its interval structure differs from C major.');
v27P('Hands and harmony','Walk through an octave','Play a C scale, steadily if you can.',['C4','D4','E4','F4','G4','A4','B4','C5'],['C5','B4','A4','G4','F4','E4','D4','C4'],'Go through every white note from C to the next C.','A major scale establishes a tonal home. Later, separate hands and finger crossings will matter.');
v27P('Reading and repertoire','Read a new pattern','Treat these letter notes as simple notation.',['G4','E4','F4','D4','C4'],['C4','F4','E4','D4','C4'],'Look at each letter, not at your last movement. Find it from a keyboard landmark.','Sight-reading means decoding unfamiliar pitches rather than memorizing the physical pattern.');
v27P('Reading and repertoire','Change the ending','A phrase can feel unresolved and then resolved.',['C4','E4','G4','B4'],['C4','E4','G4','C5'],'First ending on B; the second ends on C. Listen to the difference.','The leading tone B pulls toward C in a C-major context.');
v27P('Reading and repertoire','Play it from memory','Listen and then play the pattern; try not to depend on the labels.',['E4','F4','G4','E4','D4','C4'],['G4','A4','G4','E4','C4'],'Listen to the demo first. The notes are always available if needed.','Musical memory improves by audiating—hearing the phrase internally before you play.');
function v27Q(subject,unit,title,context,q,options,correct,why,second,secondOptions,secondCorrect,secondWhy,clue){V27_DATA[subject].push({unit,title,context,question:q,options,correct,why,second,secondOptions,secondCorrect,secondWhy,clue,type:'choice'})}
v27Q('chess','Opening judgment','Fight for the center','Both sides have developed only pawns.','What is usually a good first move for White?',['Move the queen out immediately','Play e4 or d4 to claim central space','Move a rook pawn without a reason'],1,'Central pawns gain space and make development easier.','After 1.e4 e5, which move develops a piece and attacks e5?',['Nf3','Qh5','a3'],0,'Nf3 activates the knight, attacks e5, and helps prepare castling.','A useful opening move controls the center, develops, or protects the king.');
v27Q('chess','Opening judgment','Develop before hunting','You have moved the same knight three times; the rest of your army is asleep.','What should you usually prioritize?',['Bring another piece into play','Move the knight a fourth time','Start a pawn storm by default'],0,'Development gets more pieces involved. Move one piece repeatedly only for a concrete reason.','Your king is in the center and the kingside path is clear. What might be helpful?',['Castle if legal and safe','Move the queen to h5','Ignore all threats']
